observation.visible_scene: A close side view of a moving steam locomotive's driving-wheel gear: red-painted spoked wheels with bright steel rims, joined by horizontal coupling rods, a black boiler above, a white running-board line at the top, and a thin red valve/piping rod. A large cloud of white steam/smoke billows around the wheels. A steel gantry/bridge structure is visible in the upper-left background early on.
visible_changes: The driving wheels rotate continuously (the crank pins on the coupling rods sweep through a circular cycle, the rod angle tilting and re-leveling repeatedly), indicating the locomotive is in steady motion throughout the excerpt.

The steam cloud grows, drifts, and shifts position: it starts concentrated on the left, then a dense mass builds on the right and by the late frames covers much of the right half, progressively obscuring the front wheel, cylinder and valve gear.

The camera framing tightens and re-centers on the wheelset: the top-left background gantry slides out of view, the wheels appear larger, and the locomotive body shifts leftward within the frame, so the front-end hardware becomes more hidden behind steam and the crop.
The white running-board line and boiler edge move upward in frame as the view zooms/pans toward the lower wheel mechanism.
outside_clip_unknowns: The locomotive's overall speed, direction of travel, and whether it continues moving or stops after this segment are not shown.
The source of the steam (cylinder exhaust, blower, or ambient) and what precedes/follows the crop boundaries are unseen.
uncertain_details: Exact camera motion (pan vs. track vs. zoom) cannot be cleanly separated from the train's own movement; only the net tightening and leftward shift of the subject is clear.
Direction of travel is inferred from apparent clockwise wheel rotation and steam drift, not directly confirmed.
Whether the growing right-side steam is a new emission or simply the existing cloud drifting into view is ambiguous.
